https://news.ltn.com.tw/news/focus/break.text: SAME GOALS: Taiwan’s and Germany’s memorial sites all aim to transform spaces of injustice to sites that advance human rights, said the minister’s guide, Sebastian KornerBy Huang Ching-hsuan / Staff reporter請繼續往下閱讀...Minister of Foreign Affairs Lin Chia-lung （林佳龍） in a Facebook post yesterday revealed that he had visited Germany last month and toured the Berlin Wall and the Berlin-Hohenschonhausen Memorial, among other sites.This year marks the 39th anniversary of the lifting of martial law in Taiwan, surpassing the 38-year duration of martial law, he wrote.Martial law was imposed on May 20, 1949, and lifted on July 15, 1987.“From the lifting of martial law and removal of bans on political parties and newspapers, to having direct elections for legislators and the president, Taiwan has little by little stepped out of the shadow of authoritarian rule to become the free, democratic and open country it is today,” Lin wrote.“The free air we breathe today and take for granted was fought for step by step by many democratic pioneers who used their courage, sacrifice and perseverance during a time of forced silence,” he said, adding that having been a democratic activist on campus, he appreciates Taiwan’s hard-won democracy and cherishes it.Lin wrote about his visit to Germany, including trips to the Berlin Wall and the Hohenschonhausen Memorial, a former prison used by the East German Ministry for State Security （“Stasi”） to hold political prisoners.A man named Sebastian Korner, a family member of a victim of political persecution, guided him through the memorial, from freezing cells and interrogation rooms to prisoner transport vehicles, he said.The Stasi had deployed a vast intelligence network across Germany to spy on its citizens, Lin said.It utilized isolation, intimidation and psychological torture to strip detainees of their sense of time and direction, further breaking their will and allowing authoritarian rule to penetrate every corner of people’s lives, he said.Lin said he talked with Korner about Taiwan’s White Terror history and ongoing efforts to push forward transitional justice, and recommended he watch the movie A Foggy Tale （大濛） to better understand Taiwanese’s suffering during martial law.After returning to Taiwan, Lin said he received a letter from Korner telling him that he looked up information on Taiwan and found that the Hohenschonhausen Memorial serves a similar mission as Taiwan’s Jing-Mei White Terror Memorial Park （白色恐怖景美紀念園區） and Green Island White Terror Memorial Park （白色恐怖綠島紀念園區） — transforming spaces of historical injustice into key sites that preserve memories, uncover the truth and advance human rights education, Lin said.“I also hope to have the opportunity to invite Sebastian to Taiwan in the future, to engage in exchanges on human rights education and transitional justice,” he said. “Germany and Taiwan have experienced different histories of authoritarian rule, but share a common understanding — only by revealing the truth, restoring dignity to victims and using history to educate the next generation on human rights can democracy endure and hard-won freedom be passed down.”Lin had led a delegation to attend the opening of the Taiwan Expo in Europe in Warsaw on June 22, visited the Polish Parliament on June 23, and on June 24 announced plans to establish language centers in Europe, starting in the Czech Republic, France, Germany and Poland.Lin’s trip to Germany marks another significant trip to Berlin by Taiwanese officials over the past few years. National Security Council Secretary-General Joseph Wu （吳釗燮） visited Germany in June last year, when the German Marshall Fund of the US invited him to attend the Taiwan Trilateral Forum.Wu delivered a keynote speech during the event.He also talked to German lawmakers and European policy experts on issues such as Taiwan Strait security, cooperation among democratic partners, supply chain resilience and challenges posed by the expansion of authoritarian regimes.Sources familiar with the matter said European partners have shown interest in potential cooperation with Taiwan in emerging technology areas such as uncrewed aerial vehicles and artificial intelligence. Additional reporting by Lee I-chia and CNA新聞來源：TAIPEI TIMES

Photograph: Sarah Wilson/AAP Alan Jones trial Alan Jones corresponded with 13-year-old who asked for financial help, court hears Radio host took teenager to lunch, had him visit his apartment, and told him to keep some conversations secret, court hears Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Amanda Meade Mon 5 Oct 2026 23.57 EDT Last modified on Tue 6 Oct 2026 00.08 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Alan Jones corresponded extensively with a 13-year-old who had written to him asking for financial help, showering the teenager with praise and asking him to keep some secrets from his mother. The teenager, known as complainant A, posted a letter to Jones after his father left and his single mother was struggling financially, the court heard on the first day of evidence given by complainant A in a closed court. The fifth and final complainant is one of five men who allege Jones sexually touched them between 2003 and 2020. Jones, who has pleaded not guilty to 21 charges of indecent assault and sexual touching, replied that the young correspondent was a “sophisticated, articulate 13-year-old” who was experiencing “terrible circumstances”. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email The 2GB broadcaster offered to help the family and over three years continued contact with the son over email, texts and phone calls. Jones also visited the family at home and on one occasion drove to the house but asked the teenager to come outside to meet him and did not go inside. He took the teenager to lunch alone at a pub and had him visit him at his Circular Quay apartment twice. He told the court the butler, David Allan, made him a hot breakfast on one occasion. During their lengthy correspondence Jones asked for specific details of his mother’s financial distress with housing, employment and superannuation. “I pioneered the expression ‘Struggle Street’ and I know that’s where you and your mother live,” Jones said in one of the hundreds of emails read out in the Downing Centre court on Tuesday. Alan Jones welcomed prominent athlete to luxury home with ‘hug and slap on the bottom’, former butler tells court Read more Jones signed off his emails: “Lots of love and best wishes, Alan Jones AO,” adding phrases such as “You’re always in my thoughts” and “You are a wonderful young man”. Jones asked the teenager on several occasions to keep certain details from his mother, suggesting that she was shouldering enough worry as it was. On one occasion he disclosed to the then-16-year-old that he had just signed a cheque for $86,000 for building work to his mother’s home and added: “That’s just between you and me.” Complainant A told the court he assured Jones that he was keeping certain conversations confidential, but in reality he would always tell his mother. After offering to pay for a lawyer to assist the family, Jones wrote to say that the bill was $5,500 and there were limits to his generosity and he “can’t be an endless dripping tap”. Jones wrote that “lawyers keep the meter running” and “I am not a mobile bank but I am here to help”. When the teenager suggested he and his mother start paying him back, Jones responded: “I don’t expect any of it back.” In opening statements, prosecutor Georgina Wright told the court that Jones invited the then 17-year-old complainant A to visit his farm in Fitzroy Falls in the New South Wales Southern Highlands where he allegedly kissed him on the mouth and touched him on the bottom. The trial before judge Glenn Walsh continues. PA says: The review will be led by former lord chancellor Alex Chalk and will look at “any missed opportunities to intervene”, Mahmood told the Commons. The 18-year-old died after being fatally stabbed by Vickrum Digwa in Southampton on 3 December 2025. Nowak was handcuffed as he lay dying, after Digwa, a Sikh, falsely accused him of racial abuse. In police body-worn camera footage Nowak can be heard repeatedly saying: “I’ve been stabbed,” to which an officer replies: “Don’t think you have, mate.” At Home Office questions in the Commons, Mahmood said: “I can announce an independent review led by a former lord chancellor, the right honourable Alex Chalk KC.
